title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (hedged; notation is ad hoc and the neighbouring pages are unrelated, one adelic and one a Bourbaki Tribu sheet). The data are a module omega on S, apparently S_zar for a base S of characteristic p, with two maps F_omega and V_omega. Here omega^(p) denotes the Frobenius twist; the margin reads M = omega^(p). The pattern of F and V suggests a Dieudonné-type datum such as that of a truncated Barsotti–Tate group of level 1: F: omega^(p) -> omega and V: omega -> omega^(p), with FV = 0 and VF = 0 in characteristic p. The morphism phi is plausibly the absolute Frobenius of S, or a morphism from the crystalline topos to the Zariski topos; epsilon is a restriction functor; Delta / Delta^* is some canonical complex or 'Dieudonné-type' construction. The margin gloss 'complexe can. ext. ... par omega^(p)' suggests Delta^*(omega) is a canonical extension complex.

Construction. To (omega, F, V) Grothendieck attaches four things.
(1) The pulled-back object M = phi^*(omega), with F_M = phi^*(F) and V_M = phi^*(V), and the relation epsilon^*(Delta(M)) = Delta^*(omega).
(2) A triangle T(omega) of two-term complexes: tau_0 = [omega^(p) --F--> omega] -> tau_1 -> tau_2 = [omega --V--> omega^(p)]. The middle term tau_1 has zero differential and is identified with Delta^*(omega), 'déduit de omega'. Such a triangle exists because FV = VF = 0.
(3) A canonical isomorphism alpha_omega: phi^* T(omega) ≅ T(phi^* omega).
(4) An identification beta_omega: T(omega)_1 ≅ epsilon^* Delta^*(M), a complex with zero differential.

Question. Is the functor (omega, F, V) |-> (phi^*omega, phi^*F, phi^*V, T(omega), alpha, beta) fully faithful? At least on the subcategory where F_omega = 0?

Below the rule he spells out what a morphism in the target category is:
- a map u: phi^*omega -> phi^*omega' compatible with F and V;
- a morphism of triangles v: T(omega) -> T(omega');
- the middle component v_1 is forced to equal epsilon^*(u), via the square relating beta_omega and beta_omega' to epsilon^*(u): Delta^*(omega) -> Delta^*(omega');
- phi^*(v) is forced to equal T(u), via the square with alpha_omega and alpha_omega'.

Purpose. This is a descent problem. Frobenius pullback is not fully faithful on modules (Cartier descent needs a connection). The triangle T(omega) together with its compatibilities is proposed as a substitute for the missing descent datum, to recover morphisms of (omega, F, V) from their Frobenius or crystalline pullbacks. This fits the 'Cristaux 1970' work on Dieudonné theory of BT_1 / BT groups in characteristic p.
errors: No mathematical error is detectable. The question is posed, not answered.

The definition of the middle term tau_1 is illegible and may be incomplete. If it is meant to be a single [omega^(p) --0--> omega^(p)], the ranks of a triangle with outer terms [omega^(p) -> omega] and [omega -> omega^(p)] do not obviously match; it more plausibly involves both omega and omega^(p).

ideas.what: Encoding a Dieudonné-type module (omega, F, V) in characteristic p by a distinguished triangle of two-term complexes [omega^(p) -F-> omega] -> tau_1 -> [omega -V-> omega^(p)], using FV = VF = 0
ideas.modern_name: Dieudonné modules / Dieudonné crystals of truncated BT_1 groups; F-zip-like structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1970 ICM, Montréal 1970 lectures), Messing 1972, Berthelot–Breen–Messing; F-zips: Moonen–Wedhorn
ideas.where_published: Related themes in 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (Montréal 1970/1974); this exact triangle is not known to me

ideas.what: Asking whether Frobenius (or crystalline) pullback plus triangle data with compatibility isomorphisms alpha, beta is fully faithful
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius descent / full faithfulness of the Dieudonné functor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Full faithfulness results: Berthelot–Messing, de Jong (1995), Lau, Bhatt–Lurie (recent)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck raised full-faithfulness questions for the Dieudonné functor in the Montréal lectures

missed.claim: An explicit open question: is (omega, F, V) recovered fully faithfully from its Frobenius/crystalline pullback together with a canonical triangle T(omega) and isomorphisms alpha, beta, at least when F = 0? This is a proposed replacement for a connection in Frobenius descent of Dieudonné data. It is unclear whether it was pursued.
missed.quote: Le foncteur (ω,F_ω,V_ω) ↦ (φ*(ω), φ*(F_ω), φ*(V_ω), 𝒯(ω), α_ω, β_ω) est-il pl. fidèle ?? L'est-il du moins sur la sous-catégorie des triples (ω,F_ω,V_ω) avec F_ω = 0 ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is reminiscent of current descriptions of BT_1 / Dieudonné data via derived or triangle-level structures (F-zips, prismatic and syntomic Dieudonné theory). It is only of historical interest unless the precise notation can be decoded.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a scratch page with an ad hoc construction and an open full-faithfulness question in Grothendieck's crystalline Dieudonné program. The idea of descending via a triangle is mildly interesting, but the notation is too obscure to identify a definite unrecorded result.
transcription_corrections: The margin 'M = ω^♭' is more plausibly 'M = ω^(p)' (Frobenius twist); likewise 'ω^♭' throughout should be read as ω^(p).
Item 3°: 'Iso[?] can.' is likely 'Isom can.' (canonical isomorphism).
In the lower diagram the arrow τ_1(ω) → τ_1(ω') is labelled v_1, not ω_1; the side note reads 'v_1 déterminé comme ε*(u)'.
Item 2°: the illegible symbol after '𝒯(ω)' (rendered '[?]') may be a crossed-out symbol rather than a relation.
Line 1: 'S_zar[?]' looks like 'S_zar' (Zariski site); 'on lui associe' is plausible.
Line 1: there is one marginal annotation at top right (beside the triangle) and the M = ω^(p) / ε*(Δ(M)) = Δ*(ω) note is a separate margin entry; 'complexe can. ext. de ω^? par ω^(p)' is uncertain.
